primitives.name: Individual Excellence Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: The excellence of our greatest teams—indeed,it might be said of all teams—arises from the excellence of the individual players.
primitives.assumptions: Team performance T is a function of individual excellence E_i, with diminishing returns beyond threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E_i < threshold, T approaches zero; when E_i > saturation, marginal gains in E_i do not proportionally increase T.

layer2.mapping: Individual excellence drives emergent team behavior via probabilistic modeling in GSI; in GSE, it defines action-value functions for optimal play selection.
layer2.telemetry: Player skill metrics, team win rate, and tactical consistency

primitives.name: Drill Fidelity Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is necessary to realize that perfect drill does not in itself guarantee high excellence.
primitives.assumptions: F_d is a proxy for execution consistency; E_e depends on both F_d and individual attributes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At F_d = 1, E_e may plateau due to lack of adaptability or creativity.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, F_d corresponds to model calibration accuracy; in GSE, it reflects policy stability across state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Execution consistency score, error rate during practice, and adaptive response time

The foundational principle of team excellence lies in individual capability rather than mechanical repetition. This implies that while drill fidelity ensures consistent execution, true superiority arises from superior individual attributes. The mathematical structure suggests a composite function where team performance T = f(E_i, F_d), with E_i being the dominant factor. As F_d increases toward perfection, its marginal contribution to T diminishes, indicating a non-linear relationship. The dual nature of this constraint manifests in two domains: static fidelity (F_d) and dynamic excellence (E_i). Failure occurs when either component is insufficient—either through poor training or lack of inherent talent. The epistemic lens reveals that drill serves as a necessary but insufficient condition for excellence, necessitating a Bayesian framework in GSI to estimate latent skill parameters and a state-transition model in GSE to navigate tactical evolution.
